contexts.text: Such as is the subject, such is the predicate. AC 386. AC 721. AC 4502.
Thought abstractedly from its subject is not extended; but the subject and the object of the thought are.
From the subject it is known what is predicated.
A Thing separated from its subject or substance, is nothing.
If he hangs down his hands... he is not a subject into which the Lord can operate.
For when goods are spoken of abstractedly, they are in a subject, which is a man, Spirit, or Angel.
The Spiritual does not exist without a subject.
Opposite things in one subject are never possible.
No function can be conceived of except from forms, that is, from substances; for substances are the subjects a quibus.
These things cannot be predicated without a subject, which is man.
The spirit is now thought of (as being) without any other subject than the body in which it is... and is supposed to be mere thought without an adequate subject...
The internal sense treats of all these (persons) in one subject.
These Things themselves regard one subject.
Wherever there is a subject (the Divine truth) inflows; but it is varied in the subjects according to their forms: in subjects which accord with good... But in subjects which are discordant...
For the forms or substances recipient of life, are subjects...
The case is the same with all things which are abstracted from their subjects: when they are spoken of, the subjects in which they are, are perceived. Example(s).
That the Celestial and the Spiritual are not together in one subject. References.
For the Intellectual is the subject, or containant, (of truth).
For the Intellectual is the recipient subject; and without a subject there is no reception.
For evil is in man as in its subject.
For evils and falsities have no existence except in subjects, which are men.
They who reason see scarcely anything beyond the object of the Thing about which they are reasoning, or go beyond the subject...
According to the capacity of him who is the subject. (This is object in AC 545.)

Man cannot think and will unless there is a subject which is a substance from which and in which [to do it]. That which is supposed to exist without a substantial subject, is nothing. (Thus) man cannot see without an organ which is the subject of his sight (and so on). And so with thought... and apperception... unless these were in substances and from them, which are organic forms, which are subjects, they would have no existence...

For these two faculties (the will and understanding) are the receptacles and subjects (of goods and truths); the will is the receptacle and subject of all things of good; and the understanding is the receptacle and subject of all things of truth.

They perceive love and wisdom outside the subject as flowing forth from it; and that which they perceive outside the subject as flowing forth from it they call substance and form; not knowing that love and wisdom are the subject itself; and that that which is perceived outside of it as volatile and fluent is only an appearance of the state of the subject in itself. DLW 40:end.

The subject of touch is the skin... The sense of touch is not in the things which are applied; but is in the skin's substance and form, which are the subject... So with taste... the tongue is the subject. (And so on.)

(Thus) the affection of the substance and form which causes sense, is not anything separated from the subject; but only causes a change in it, the subject remaining the subject then, as before, and afterwards. (Thus) seeing, hearing, etc., are not anything volatile which flows forth from their organs; but are the organs themselves regarded in their substance and form...

All the affections, perceptions, and thoughts (in the brain) are not exhalations from these substances; but are actually and really the subjects, which emit nothing from themselves; but only undergo changes according to the things which flow to and affect them.
The Divine is not in one subject differently from hat it is in another; but one created subject is different from another...

The conjunction of the Creator with the created universe... is not possible unless there are subjects in which His Divine can be as in itself; thus in which it can dwell and abide. In order that these subjects may be His dwelling-places, they must be recipients of His love and wisdom as of themselves... These subjects are men...
All perfections increase according to degrees... because all predicates follow their subjects; and perfection and imperfection are general predicates...

Affection and thought, charity and faith, will and understanding (are like) love and wisdom, in that they are not possible outside of subjects which are substances, but are states of subjects, that is, of substances. DLW 224:end.
From its being possible to think of (these) abstractedly from the substances which are their subjects... a right idea about them, as being states of substances or forms, has perished. Explained.
The conatuses, forces, and motions in dead and living subjects. Explained.
Living conatus in man, who is a living subject...
Such a form supposes a substantial form as a subject; for without a substantial form as a subject, changes of state are impossible...
The subjects of the animal kingdom... The subjects of the vegetable kingdom... DLW 346:2.

Affections and thoughts do not exist except in substances and their forms, which are subjects; and, as they exist in the brains, which is full of substances and forms, they are called forms purely organic. Explained.
Like things exist in the organic forms of the mind, which are the subjects of the affection and thoughts. Explained.
Subjects which should receive the Divine more nearly...
Good can be turned into evil by the recipient subject... Such a subject is man as to his proprium...
There exists no operation except into a subject, and through means into it...
There exists neither good nor truth which is not in a substance as in its subject... (See Substance.)
That good and truth... are in created subjects according to the form of each. Explained.
In the subjects of the animal kingdom...

All man's affections and thoughts are in forms, and thence from forms; for forms are their subjects. If affections and thoughts were not in subjects, which have been formed, they would be possible in skulls empty of brains...
The expanse around the Sun of Heaven... is in the extense of the natural sun, and is with living subjects there according to the receptions; and the receptions are according to the forms.
That the evil are evil, and evil things evil, lies in the subjects and objects themselves...
So with every subject of a lower sort in the animal kingdom...
When I say subject and predicate, it means that the predicates, that is, the things which are predicated, must be applied to that which the subject signifies, as in the Prophets. Explained.

They have no idea of any substance which is a subject of thought... Thought cannot be without a subject... They who suppose a Spirit to be mere thought without a substance which is a subject, are mistaken...
A Spirit is... a subtle organic substance, which is the subject of thought...
a. In the middle, and thus in the light, is the Thing which is the subject.

For the will is the subject and receptacle of charity, as it is the subject and receptacle of good; and the understanding is the subject and receptacle of faith, because it is the subject and receptacle of truth.

For the Lord's life is in man as the light and heat of the sun are in a subject; which are not of the subject, but are of the sun in it... Still, when they are in the subject, they apparently wholly belong to it... Man is the recipient subject...

As the understanding sees from the light of Heaven, it is evident that it is a subject and a receptacle of that light; thus also is a subject and a receptacle of truth... And, as the will loves from the heat of Heaven, it is evident that it is a subject and a receptacle of that heat, thus also is a subject and a receptacle of good, thus of love.
(Thus) the objects or ends of affections are uses, and therefore their subjects are uses.
As there is no affection without its subject, so there is no affection of man's life without use.
2. The will is not any abstract spiritual thing; but is a subject substantiated and formed for the reception of love. (The same with the understanding.)

5. In all things of his thought and speech, and of his will and action, the natural man has as his subject, matter, space, time, and quantity... The spiritual man does not have these as subjects; but only as objects. Explained.
2. The subjects (of the Angels) are those things from which (spiritual objects) appear, which are such things as are of wisdom and love. Example(s).
God. 5. The Divine love... wills that it be in a subject...
God. 8. 11. Evils are outside of the subjects...
